problem: Multi-modal retrieval-augmented generation (MRAG) systems retrieve visual evidence from large image corpora that frequently contain human faces with sensitive personal identity information, creating a fundamental tension between protecting privacy and preserving non-identity visual cues required for downstream reasoning by large multi-modal models (p.1). Existing anonymization techniques either destroy critical spatial and semantic structure (like gaze, expression, and pose) or fail to provide principled privacy guarantees against identity recovery (p.1).
methodology: The paper proposes Identity-Decoupled MRAG, a framework that interposes a generative anonymization module between the retrieval and generation stages consisting of three components: (i) a disentangled variational encoder that factorizes each face into an identity code and a spatially-structured attribute code regularized by a mutual-information penalty and a gradient-based independence term; (ii) a manifold-aware rejection sampler that replaces the identity code with a synthetic, distinct, and realistic code from a reference gallery; and (iii) a conditional latent diffusion generator synthesized into a Latent Consistency Model for low-latency deployment, with privacy enforced via a multi-oracle ensemble of face recognition models using a hinge-based loss (p.1-2, p.5).
dataset: Three distinct datasets were utilized to evaluate generalization: (i) CelebA-RAG, a controlled benchmark adapted from CelebA with 10,000 high-resolution images, 2,000 text queries, and disjoint identity partitions; (ii) LFW-Wild-RAG, an in-the-wild benchmark built on Labeled Faces in the Wild encompassing 13,233 images and 5,749 identities; and (iii) FairFace-RAG (p.5).
results: On the CelebA-RAG benchmark, the proposed method with 50-step DDPM achieved a Decoupled Attack Rate (DAR) of 1.8%, L2 Distance of 1.95, VQA Accuracy of 86.4%, Gaze Estimation Error of 2.8 degrees, FID of 10.1, LPIPS of 0.075, and Latency of 845.0 ms, while the 4-step LCM variant achieved a DAR of 2.8%, L2 Distance of 1.85, VQA Accuracy of 85.4%, Gaze Error of 3.5 degrees, FID of 11.2, LPIPS of 0.082, and Latency of 42.3 ms (p.6). On the LFW-Wild-RAG benchmark, the 50-step DDPM achieved a DAR of 2.5%, L2 Distance of 1.81, VQA Accuracy of 82.3%, Gaze Error of 3.5 degrees, FID of 13.5, LPIPS of 0.091, and Latency of 845.0 ms, whereas the 4-step LCM achieved a DAR of 3.5%, L2 Distance of 1.72, VQA Accuracy of 81.2%, Gaze Error of 4.2 degrees, FID of 14.8, LPIPS of 0.105, and Latency of 42.3 ms (p.6).
key_findings: The proposed ID-Decoupled MRAG framework successfully shifts the privacy-utility Pareto frontier, outperforming heuristic blur and pixelation baselines as well as alternative generative approaches by simultaneously suppressing identity leakage and maintaining high VQA accuracy and gaze estimation fidelity (p.6). Furthermore, distilling the conditional latent diffusion generator into a 4-step Latent Consistency Model drastically reduces inference latency to 42.3 ms while maintaining competitive performance against the 50-step DDPM variant (p.6).
title: Identity-Decoupled Anonymization for Visual Evidence in Multi-modal Retrieval-Augmented Generation
